reliable_uses: Vicious Syndicate Data Reaper reports provide current meta-level matchup spreads, archetype popularity, and rank-segmented performance that can seed matchup posture assumptions and source-backed archetype confidence.

Vicious Syndicate day-1 and deck overview articles provide human-written game plans, likely mulligan anchors, synergy notes, and likely win conditions for new archetypes before large replay samples exist.
HSReplay archetype and deck surfaces plus Mulligan G-V2 provide data-backed opening-hand guidance, per-deck or per-archetype mulligan context, and matchup-oriented deck discovery for Standard lists.

HSGuru deck pages, card stats, archetype stats, matchup tabs, and replay links help identify exact list variants, archetype labels, and card-level impact signals that can support role tagging and low-confidence matchup posture.
HearthSim Deckstrings documentation and reference libraries provide deterministic decode and encode behavior for deck codes, including hero, format, and DBF-based card lists.
HearthstoneJSON provides machine-readable card IDs, dbfId mapping, card text, mechanics, type, class, and play-requirement metadata needed to join decoded deckstrings to card semantics.
limitations: Vicious Syndicate day-1 deck articles are theorycrafted and explicitly not a replacement for post-launch, data-backed refinement.
HSReplay Mulligan G-V2 is Standard-only according to its FAQ, so it should not be treated as full Wild or all-format coverage.
HSReplay and HSGuru statistics reflect tracker-user populations rather than the full ladder population; low-sample windows and fresh-patch periods can overfit rare lists.
HSGuru matchup analysis relies on card-play-based archetype classification because the opponent's exact list is unknown, so similar archetypes can blur together.
Deckstring specifications and card metadata can decode and describe cards, but they cannot infer matchup plans, combo timing, or safe VisionAI targets by themselves.
None of these online sources prove HearthRanger config load, runtime correctness, or gameplay improvement; Step 1 remains static research only.
relevant_config_surfaces: outputs/<deck_slug>/config_preview/<deck_slug>/Combo.json only when exact sequencing is source-backed
architectural_implications: Separate three pipelines: deckstring decoding, card metadata hydration, and strategy or archetype inference. Only the first two are deterministic; the third must stay confidence-scored and source-cited.

Store source claims at card-level and archetype-level separately so a deck can inherit general archetype posture while exact-list card roles still depend on the decoded cards present in the submitted list.
Require patch, format, and retrieval-date stamping on all community-guide claims because mulligan advice and matchup posture drift quickly after balance patches and expansions.
Use consensus weighting: prefer high-confidence static semantics only when a guide source such as Vicious Syndicate and a data source such as HSReplay or HSGuru point in the same direction.

Map unsupported symbolic advice, such as flexible face-versus-trade heuristics, into gameplan or suppression-report artifacts first; emit runtime Mulligan or Combo rows only when the claim can be translated into documented VisionAI syntax.

Treat exact deck identity and archetype identity as separate contracts: the submitted deckstring should remain immutable, while archetype inference can be revised when newer public data changes classification.
recommended_contracts: source_evidence_index.json: normalized source registry with url, source_family, retrieved_at, patch_or_expansion, format, access_notes, and per-claim confidence.
deckstring_decode_receipt.json: deck_code, hero_dbf_id, format, canonical_card_dbf_ids, and decode library or spec version.
card_metadata_snapshot.json: card_id, dbfId, cost, class, type, mechanics, text, playRequirements, and locale or build provenance for every decoded card.

archetype_research.json: archetype label, confidence, primary win conditions, mulligan anchors, board and resource posture, face-versus-trade rules, known bad patterns, unsupported mechanics, and source refs.
card_role_map.json: every decoded deck card mapped to one or more role tags with evidence refs and confidence.
card_usage_expectations.json: hold, play, target, and resource expectations per card, with matchup-conditioned rows separated from unconditional rows.
matchup_posture_assumptions.json: default posture plus opponent archetype-conditioned posture rows, each evidence-gated and explicitly low-confidence when sample sizes are weak.
config_surface_intent_map.json: claims translated into intended surfaces such as Mulligan.json, GlobalValues.json, CARDID.json, Combo.json, or report-only suppression.
archetype_identification_receipt.json: exact deck list, matched archetype source, confidence, and ambiguity notes.
never_autogenerate_without: A successful deckstring decode and card-metadata join for every card in the submitted deck code.
A source_evidence_index entry for every archetype, mulligan, matchup, or card-role claim used by the generator.
At least one current guide-style source and one current data-style source for any high-confidence mulligan or matchup posture claim.
Explicit downgrade to low confidence or contract_gap when sources disagree, are stale for the current patch, or do not cover the exact list.
Validation that every decoded card is covered in card_role_map.json and card_usage_expectations.json.
A preview-only pass that validates deck_research_contract.json, gameplan_contract.json, and config preview artifacts before any guarded write-runtime step.
Human-visible suppression or gap reporting for claims that cannot be translated into documented Mulligan.json, Combo.json, GlobalValues.json, or CARDID.json syntax.
Acceptance authority from local Step 1 reports before any live runtime apply; online research alone is not sufficient.
